name: Historical Evidence for the Resurrection

objectives.text: Retell that the women found the tomb of Jesus empty on the first day of the week
Name people who saw Jesus alive after He rose, such as Mary Magdalene, Peter, and the disciples
Identify ways the risen Jesus showed His followers that He had a real body, such as eating fish and inviting them to touch Him
Sequence the events of Easter morning using the Gospel accounts
Describe how the disciples changed from hiding in fear to preaching boldly in public after the resurrection
Explain why the willingness of the apostles to suffer for their testimony shows that they sincerely believed they had seen the risen Jesus
Explain why the Gospels naming women as the first witnesses of the empty tomb supports the honesty of the accounts
Compare the swoon theory with the Gospel details about the death and burial of Jesus
Explain why Paul teaches that the Christian faith depends on whether Jesus actually rose from the dead in history
Explain what the early creed in 1 Corinthians 15 records and why its early date matters as historical evidence
Analyze the minimal facts approach by identifying the facts about the death and resurrection of Jesus that most historians accept and how they point to the resurrection
Analyze how the conversions of the skeptic James and the persecutor Paul function as evidence for the resurrection
Analyze how the rapid rise of the church in Jerusalem and the shift to worship on the first day of the week point to the reality of the resurrection
Evaluate the stolen body theory using the account of the guarded tomb and the report of the guards
Apply historical criteria such as multiple attestation, early testimony, and enemy attestation to the resurrection accounts
Evaluate the hallucination theory in light of the group appearances and physical encounters reported in the New Testament
Defend the Reformed confession of a bodily resurrection against spiritualized interpretations using the biblical texts
Compare how evidential and presuppositional approaches within the Reformed tradition use historical evidence for the resurrection
Construct a written historical case for the resurrection that presents the evidence and answers major alternative theories

changes: Kept and reworded the empty tomb, eyewitnesses, physical body, Easter sequence, disciples' transformation, martyrdom, swoon, minimal facts, James and Paul, early church, stolen body, hallucination, bodily resurrection, and historical case objectives with verse-level anchors. Reframed 'apply to our own hope' as explaining why Paul ties faith to the historical event, avoiding an inner-experience objective. Dropped the Trilemma essay as it concerns the identity of Jesus rather than resurrection evidence. Added the women as first witnesses, the early creed of 1 Corinthians 15, historical criteria, and a comparison of evidential and presuppositional uses of evidence in the Reformed tradition. Added WCF 8.4, WSC Q28, HC Q45, and WCF 1.5 where they state the doctrine taught.
